races.title: State House, District 17
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Frank Iler
cands.bio: Republican state House member for District 17 (Brunswick County) since 2009, when he was appointed after Bonner Stiller resigned. Business graduate of Campbell University. Former cost accountant and budget supervisor in textiles, fast-food franchise owner, and sales and marketing worker. Brunswick Community College trustee 2007–2025.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or details of his early life before he came to North Carolina at 14. We found no stated position from him on data centers, development limits, homestead property taxes, out-of-state or investor land buying, school choice or teacher pay, or limits on donor money. His campaign site offers only general statements on guns, abortion and policing, with no specific bills. We found no controversies, foreign ties or endorsements in the pages available. The bills he has sponsored were not available for review.

local.label: Roots 80: His campaign site says he came to North Carolina at age fourteen and graduated from Greensboro Senior High School, and he has lived in Brunswick County for about 25 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the NC House since 2009 and has been vice chair of Appropriations and chair of the Transportation and Transportation Appropriations committees. Earlier he was a cost accountant and budget supervisor in the textile industry and owned a fast-food franchise.
qual.why: Eight terms of legislative service plus an accounting and budget career and business ownership put him in the high range. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Eight terms of legislative service plus an accounting and budget career and business ownership put him in the high range. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he voted to pass House Bill 318, the Illegal Alien Enforcement Act, which requires jails and courts to check immigration status of people accused of serious crimes.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says the Second Amendment protects a fundamental right and must be defended.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says public safety is job one and that law enforcement must be supported.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says 'We must protect the sanctity of all human life.' It does not give specific abortion policies.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he came to North Carolina at age fourteen and graduated from Greensboro Senior High School, and he has lived in Brunswick County for about 25 years.

cands.name: Dennis A. Breen
cands.bio: Dennis A. Breen is a lawyer admitted in North Carolina and New York with nearly four decades of practice: 24 years in insurance defense and 15 years in plaintiff's personal injury work. He holds no prior public office. He was the 2026 Democratic nominee for NC House District 17.
cands.gaps: We could not find the year Breen moved to North Carolina. He has held no public office, so there are no legislative actions to report. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, or police pay and public-order laws. Everything above on his positions comes from his own campaign site and Ballotpedia survey, which are statements, not actions.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lawyer for about 40 years, with 24 years in insurance defense litigation and 15 in plaintiff's personal injury work. He co-authored a legal text and wrote for the New York Law Journal. He has not held elected office.
qual.why: A long legal career puts him in the middle band for a lawmaker. He has no legislative, policy-staff or budget experience, and no local elected office.
qual.label: A long legal career puts him in the middle band for a lawmaker. He has no legislative, policy-staff or budget experience, and no local elected office.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he supports universal background checks, red flag laws and safe storage requirements.

pro-life.evidence: Says he opposes further abortion restrictions and wants to restore access beyond the current 12-week ban.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he will keep zoning and land-use decisions local, require infrastructure to keep pace with growth, protect trees, wetlands and natural buffers, and limit special-interest influence in development decisions.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says uncontrolled development has choked the community and that growth must be controlled so infrastructure, schools and drains keep up. He also says green space and tree loss cause flooding, and he favors planned growth with workforce housing.
